question: An indifference map is a collection of indifference curves that represent different levels of __ __ .
solution:
The correct answer is __**satisfaction**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• An **indifference map** is a collection of indifference curves, each representing different levels of **satisfaction** or utility derived from consuming combinations of two goods.
 
• Each curve on the map corresponds to a specific level of satisfaction, with higher curves representing higher levels of satisfaction.
 
• The map illustrates how a consumer might trade one good for another while maintaining the same level of satisfaction.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Demand
 
• Indifference maps are not directly related to demand.
 
• Demand reflects how much of a good a consumer is willing and able to purchase at a given price, which depends on the consumer's preferences, budget, and prices.
 
• While preferences are depicted by an indifference map, it does not directly show the demand for goods.
 
• Supply
 
• Supply refers to the quantity of a good or service that producers are willing and able to offer at various prices.
 
• An indifference map focuses on consumer preferences and satisfaction, not production or supply.
 
• Consumption
 
• While an indifference map deals with combinations of goods consumed, it is not primarily about the act of consumption.
 
• Instead, it focuses on the level of satisfaction (utility) that a consumer derives from those combinations of goods.
